thesis.description: What will the spot rental price of an hour of Nvidia H100 GPU compute average over calendar 2026, after peaking around $3.20/hour in May 2026 and then declining?
thesis.outcome: The realized spot rental price for an hour of H100 GPU time over calendar 2026, versus the ~$3.20/hour May 2026 peak.
thesis.period: Calendar 2026 (check date 2026-12-31); set from the item's reported May-2026 peak (~$3.20/hour) and subsequent decline in the H100 spot-rate series.

thesis.description: What share of Chinese companies' AI accelerator spending will go to domestic suppliers over the 12 months following July 2026, versus the 46% planned in the Bloomberg Intelligence survey?
thesis.outcome: The realized share of Chinese enterprises' AI accelerator budget captured by domestic suppliers (Huawei, Hygon, Cambricon and others) over the 12 months from mid-2026, measured against the 46% planned and the 30% current level.
thesis.period: The 12 months from the survey's release on 2026-07-07 (to mid-2027); settled when follow-up survey or market-share data covering that period are published.

thesis.description: How much will the top U.S. hyperscalers spend on custom AI accelerators (ASIC/XPU chips such as those Marvell designs for Amazon and Microsoft) in calendar 2026, and how much AI-accelerator demand is bypassing NVIDIA GPUs?
thesis.outcome: The dollar volume of hyperscaler custom-ASIC purchases in calendar 2026 (as reflected in the ASIC vendors' custom AI silicon revenue) versus those hyperscalers' NVIDIA GPU purchases — a measure of how far AI compute is shifting from NVIDIA GPUs to custom silicon for inference.
thesis.period: Calendar year 2026 (this calendar year relative to the 14 July 2026 item), checked against ASIC vendors' and hyperscalers' calendar-2026 disclosures in early 2027.

thesis.description: How much equity will NVIDIA hold in Intel, and at what total committed amount, at NVIDIA's next annual report, following its $5 billion equity investment in Intel?
thesis.outcome: The size and carrying amount of NVIDIA's equity stake in Intel, and any additional commitment, disclosed at NVIDIA's next annual report.
thesis.period: NVIDIA's next annual report (FY2027 Form 10-K, expected early 2027); the investment is already undertaken, so it is tracked by its amount at the next annual report.

thesis.description: Will the spot price for an hour on an Nvidia H100 GPU continue to fall through calendar 2026, extending the drop from its May 2026 peak of about $3.20?
thesis.outcome: Direction of the H100 GPU hourly spot rental price through calendar 2026, specifically whether it remains below the ~$3.20/hour May 2026 peak and continues the steady decline.
thesis.period: Year-end 2026; set as the check date for whether the H100 spot price remains below the May 2026 peak of about $3.20/hour, using Ornn/compute marketplace spot price data.

thesis.description: What share of Chinese enterprises' AI accelerator spending will go to domestic suppliers (Huawei, Hygon, Cambricon and others) over the 12 months from mid-2026, and how far will Nvidia's share of the Chinese accelerator market fall from its present level?
thesis.outcome: The share of Chinese enterprises' AI accelerator budgets allocated to domestic products versus the ~30% baseline reported in the July 2026 Bloomberg Intelligence survey, and the direction of Nvidia's share of that market, as reported in follow-up surveys and Nvidia's disclosed China revenue.
thesis.period: The 12 months following the survey's release on 2026-07-07 (through roughly mid-2027); set by the survey's stated 'next 12 months' horizon, checked against follow-up Bloomberg Intelligence surveys and Nvidia's quarterly China revenue disclosures over that window.

thesis.description: What will happen to HBM/DRAM contract prices over the 12 months to mid-2027, after rising roughly tenfold over the past year and becoming the data-center bottleneck?
thesis.outcome: The change in HBM/DRAM contract prices over the 12 months to mid-2027, versus the roughly tenfold rise over the prior year.
thesis.period: The 12 months to 2027-06-30 (next calendar year); set from the item's report that memory prices rose tenfold over the past year and its view that conditions will persist absent an HBM breakthrough.

thesis.description: How much will DRAM, NAND and high-bandwidth memory contract prices rise in calendar 2026, and what will the memory content of NVIDIA's Vera Rubin VR200 rack cost, now that memory is reported to be 25-30% of the rack bill of materials?
thesis.outcome: The direction and size of 2026 memory contract price increases and the memory cost per NVIDIA Vera Rubin rack (Morgan Stanley currently puts memory content at about $2 million per rack, up 435%), which bears on NVIDIA's per-rack cost/ASP economics and on hyperscaler AI-infrastructure spending.
thesis.period: Calendar year 2026 — checked against memory contract price releases and NVIDIA/partner disclosures of rack bill-of-materials as Vera Rubin ramps during H2 2026.

thesis.description: Will the US government keep in force, broaden, or tighten its approval allowing Nvidia to sell some of its semiconductors to China under specified conditions, and at what scale will those permitted China sales occur?
thesis.outcome: Whether US export-control approval for Nvidia semiconductor sales to China remains in force, is expanded, or is restricted, and the resulting scale of Nvidia's permitted China sales.
thesis.period: Fiscal year ending late January 2027 (reported ~February 2027); set as the current fiscal year-end for a pending regulatory decision, checked against US export-control rule updates and Nvidia's China revenue disclosure.

thesis.description: How much will U.S. federal agencies obligate in AI-related spending in calendar/fiscal 2026, and how much in new AI-related contract awards will be recorded?
thesis.outcome: The total AI-related spending obligated by U.S. federal agencies in 2026 (reported at $7.2 billion so far, versus $675 million in 2024) and the value of potential AI contract awards (reported at $91.8 billion, versus $4.6 billion in 2024).
thesis.period: Calendar/fiscal 2026; settled by year-end 2026 U.S. federal procurement data (e.g., USAspending.gov) reporting total AI-related obligations and contract awards. Set from the item's 2026 obligations figure ($7.2 billion) and potential-awards figure ($91.8 billion).

thesis.description: How much will NVIDIA have invested in Firmus Technologies, and what equity stake will it hold, following its reported ~$500 million ($721 million) subscription to Firmus' $2.9 billion equity raising, once Firmus lists on the ASX?
thesis.outcome: The amount NVIDIA invests and the equity stake it holds in Firmus Technologies after its preference shares convert to ordinary equity at Firmus' ASX IPO.
thesis.period: Firmus' ASX listing later in 2026 (preference shares convert to ordinary equity there); the stake is already undertaken, so it is also tracked by its amount at NVIDIA's next annual report (FY2027 Form 10-K, expected early 2027). Set from the item's 'later this year' listing timing, within 18 months of the 2026-07-08 item.
